definitions.explanation: Indicates the highest degree of something. Somewhat literary or formal in tone. Often used with adjectives or adjectival nouns to intensify meaning.

examples.japanese: {至極|しごく}{当然|とうぜん}のことだ。
あなたの{意見|いけん}は{至極|しごく}もっともだ。
{彼|かれ}の{説明|せつめい}は{至極|しごく}{簡潔|かんけつ}で{分|わ}かりやすく、{聞|き}いている{全員|ぜんいん}が{納得|なっとく}した。
examples.english: His explanation was extremely concise and easy to understand, and everyone listening was convinced.

notes:
USAGE NOTE:
A somewhat formal or literary intensifier. The most common collocation by far is {至極|しごく}{当然|とうぜん} (perfectly natural/obvious) and {至極|しごく}もっとも (entirely reasonable). Less commonly used than {非常|ひじょう}に or とても in everyday speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {至極|しごく}{当然|とうぜん} (perfectly natural)
- {至極|しごく}もっとも (entirely reasonable)
- {至極|しごく}{簡単|かんたん} (extremely simple)
- {至極|しごく}{真|まっと}うな (very proper/legitimate)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {非常|ひじょう}に: extremely (standard formal intensifier)
- {極|きわ}めて: extremely (formal, written)
- とても: very (casual, everyday)
